step.text:
The issue is that `ChatMessage` currently reads `agentSeed` by matching the item's author ID against available agents, but for helper threads the author is the parent agent (like Bubbles) rather than the helper itself (like Copy). Jamel wants the helper's name and mark to be used instead. Since `ThreadItem` already has author information but the mark is a `SubagentMark`, I need to find the cleanest way to surface the helper's identity through the existing codebase structure.

I'm weighing two approaches: either add a helper field directly to `ThreadItem` so `ChatMessage` can render the `SubagentMark` when present, or have `buildThread` accept an optional identity override that applies the helper name and mark to all agent-authored items in that thread. The second option feels cleaner since it's a single configuration point, and only `SubagentRun` would need to pass this override. But there's a subtlety—the helper's thread also contains the person's own messages if they steer via the composer, and those should stay attributed to the person, not the helper. Only agent-authored items like replies, thinking, and tool calls should get the helper identity, while note items stay as crew.

For the implementation, I need to substitute the helper name where `labelOf(event.agentId, event.agentLabel)` is currently used for agent start and end steps, and set a helper seed field on those items so the mark renders. Steps don't show avatars—only reply items do through `ChatMessage`—so the change is really just for replies. There's also a question about whether wrapping the helper name in `MemberName` makes sense, since hovering would show the agent's card but the name says something else, which could be confusing. Keeping it simple might mean not wrapping it in `MemberName` when it's a helper.

Looking at the design rules, agents always render their deterministic generated pet icon, never an avatar. A helper is different and should get its own generated mark. So the approach is to add a `helperSeed` field to `ThreadItem`, and when it's set, `ChatMessage` draws the helper mark instead of the agent icon, with the name rendered plain text rather than wrapped in `MemberName`. Then `buildThread` gets an optional parameter to specify the identity the agent's words should read under in that thread.

Now I need to check all the call sites for `buildThread` to see how adding this parameter would affect them, and review the `StepRow` implementation.

**The placeholder**

A field is `user-select: text` so it can be typed in, and a placeholder sits inside that field, so a select all painted a band over the app's own words in every empty box. It is shut now while the box is empty, and it opens again on the first keystroke. A click and a keystroke both still land, checked in a real window.

Two reasons it survived the last pass. A placeholder is **painted over and never copied**, so anything that reads the selection back sees an empty string and says all is well. And the fix cannot live in the base layer with the rest: tldraw ships an unlayered `input { user-select: text }`, and a rule in no layer beats every layer whatever either side is written with, so inside the layer the fix would have worked until somebody opened a board and stopped working from then on. Measured, not reasoned: layered comes out `text`, unlayered comes out `none`. It is the one plain rule in the file and it says why.

**The rest of the list**

I rendered the thread bar, the files changed card, the panel tabs and the board empty state class for class inside their real ancestors, against the real compiled stylesheet, and drove a drag, a select all and a bitmap diff over each one. All of them compute `user-select: none` and move zero pixels. The window in your screenshot was running the renderer from before the change, which also explains why the top bar was the one part that looked right in it.

The side panel wraps a whole thread in `select-text`, so every step row, helper chip, reaction pill, message header, timestamp and count drawn in it was selectable. The panel inherits its background from the parent container, which is likely `ink-900` from `AsideView`. Since `ScrollFade` is already used consistently across similar panels like `TasksPanel` and `PlanView`, I'll keep it as-is.

Now I'm building the SubagentList component with a Row subcomponent that displays each subagent run with a mark, subject text, and loading state, then wrapping the list in ScrollFade with scroll edge detection.

I'm reconsidering the layout structure — the parent ScreenSwap with fill likely uses absolute positioning, so I need to make sure SubagentList's outer container is relative with full height, then nest the scrollable div inside to avoid layout conflicts.

Now I'm looking at how helper identity works in the thread system — ThreadItem gets an optional helperSeed field, and buildThread accepts an `as` parameter with name and seed to track which helper generated the work, so entries are attributed correctly under the helper's own identity rather than the parent agent's.

In the spoke function, I'm checking whether we're in a helper context — if so, use the helper's name and seed, otherwise use the agent's label and ID. Then I need to refactor how stepItem gets called so it receives the computed author name from spoke, which means extracting that first before building the item.

For agent.end, I'm pushing a reply object and need to be careful about the order of spread operations — spoke's author and authorId fields should come before the explicit agentId assignment to avoid unintended overwrites. Also need to check the thread.ag reference.

In the chat message rendering, I'm conditionally showing either a linked time display, a SubagentMark if there's a helperSeed, an AgentIcon if there's an agentSeed, or a regular Avatar with the author name. For SubagentRun, I'm memoizing the helper object from the thread data.

Now for the header section, I'm building the SubagentPanel header with a screen swap button that toggles between back and top views depending on whether we're inside a helper thread, along with a tooltip and button for navigating to all helpers. I'm reconsidering what "left-aligned with the back chevron" actually means. It could mean the text sits on the same row as the chevron, or it could mean the text's left edge aligns with where the chevron starts. Looking at the current layout, the chevron takes up its own row and the description is indented below it, but maybe the intent is to remove that indent so the text starts flush at the same horizontal position as the chevron. The description line could sit beside the chevron on the same row, which matches the ScreenSwap pattern and uses space efficiently. But "left-aligned with the back chevron" suggests they should share a left edge, meaning the description sits below. Maybe Jamel means the whole header row—chevron plus description—should start at the left edge, which could work either way depending on how it's interpreted. So the first layout—chevron and subject on one line with the divider below—is the stronger design choice and matches what he meant by "at the top" and "just have the line." I'll go with that and note the decision.
